requirements.requirement: Web application container runs as the unprivileged account appsvc
requirements.summary: appsvc created as a regular (non-root) locked-password user (uid 1000), with rootless podman running the container under appsvc's own systemd --user manager. podman ps confirms container 'webapp' owned by appsvc's session before and after reboot.

curl to node1:8080 returns HTTP 200 with httpd content both before and after reboot; listening-sockets snapshot confirms port 8080 listening (pasta.avx2, the rootless podman port-forwarder) after executor changes, absent before.

requirements.requirement: Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
requirements.summary: loginctl enable-linger appsvc set Linger=yes; webapp.service enabled under appsvc's systemd --user manager. A real reboot was performed (boot_id changed from 5f3ce3b8-... to 7839216f-...), and after reconnect the container, user@1000.service, and webapp.service were all active/enabled again with confirmed absence of any appsvc login session both before and after reboot, and HTTP 8080 responded post-reboot.

overall_summary: The task's material outcomes are all satisfied with direct evidence: a rootless podman container serving httpd on port 8080 runs under the unprivileged appsvc account, and a genuine reboot (with boot_id change and reconnect) demonstrates the service, container, and HTTP endpoint recover automatically post-boot while appsvc has no active login session (via systemd linger). The single managed node's restart-evidence protocol is fully and coherently captured, matching the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots. The only blemish is minor leftover temp files (setup script and logs) in /tmp, a low-severity hygiene issue.
limitations: Only one managed node (node1) exists, so the node-restart evidence protocol and the task's own boot-recovery requirement fully overlap; no additional nodes were available to cross-check restart evidence quality independently.
cmd-d1e40ad9dcf44244's rc=3 failure mode is inferred from context (likely a SIGPIPE from a piped `head` under `set -e pipefail`) since no stderr was captured for that command.
No explicit confirmation that the leftover /tmp files (setup_webapp.sh, dnf.log, reboot.log) were intentionally retained or simply forgotten; they represent low-risk but unremoved residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (podman install, appsvc creation, passwd lock, loginctl enable-linger, systemd user unit creation, enable+start of webapp.service, systemctl reboot) map directly to satisfying the task contract or collecting required restart evidence. The first setup attempt (cmd-d1e40ad9dcf44244) exited non-zero (rc=3) partway through (likely a SIGPIPE from `... | head -5` under `set -e pipefail`), but the mutations it made (package install, user creation, linger) were idempotent and were safely completed by the corrective rerun (cmd-27d2ee01c2c347fe) rather than reverted — a corrective continuation, not an unnecessary mutation. Minor residue was left behind: /tmp/setup_webapp.sh, /tmp/dnf.log, and /tmp/reboot.log remain in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot with no evidence of cleanup. No failed services, no unexpected port exposure beyond the required 8080, and package-health checks are clean before and after.
